questions.stem: A cactus has spines instead of broad leaves. How does this adaptation help it survive in a desert?

options.text: Spines absorb more sunlight for photosynthesis
Spines store water inside them for use during droughts
Spines attract pollinators in desert environments
Spines have a much smaller surface area than leaves, greatly reducing water loss by transpiration

questions.explanation: By having spines instead of broad, flat leaves, cacti dramatically reduce their surface area exposed to the air. Since transpiration occurs mainly through the leaf surface, having a very small surface area means far less water is lost through evaporation.
